subject.title: feat(browser): send pages to OpenClaw from the Chrome extension

question: Should the official Chrome extension gain a page-sharing workflow that may deliver explicitly selected page or Google Docs text to the main agent session, and should Gateway-hosted plugins receive the new public main-session resolver to support it?
rationale: The patch is a feature addition with a new browser permission/data-flow boundary and an additive SDK commitment; correctness evidence cannot determine whether those are desired permanent product contracts.

options.title: Approve the extension capability and SDK seam
options.body: Accept page sharing as an official Chrome-extension feature and retain the documented public resolver as the supported Gateway-hosted plugin contract.

options.title: Keep the feature but revise the SDK boundary
options.body: Approve the user workflow while asking for a more generic existing or newly designed plugin-service/session contract before merging.

options.title: Defer official page sharing
options.body: Keep this capability outside the bundled extension until maintainers want to own its privacy, permission, and support surface.

recommendation.title: Approve the extension capability and SDK seam
recommendation.body: Accept page sharing as an official Chrome-extension feature and retain the documented public resolver as the supported Gateway-hosted plugin contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history identifies this person as the active contributor across the affected browser relay and SDK proposal, though a dedicated merged-main owner was not established from the supplied context.
